1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
2	
3	> Status: draft v3, for owner review · Updated: 2026-11-09
4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
5	> what it gives Compliance.
6	
7	## How to read this
8	
9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
12	
13	| Marker | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes and links the official page. |
16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
19	
20	Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
21	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
22	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
23	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
24	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
25	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. The decision in one page
30	
31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
33	
34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
35	
36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h, layer 7) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
41	
42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
43	|---|---|
44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, OD1, OD6; storage conditions [design], layer 5). |
46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
48	
49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
50	
51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an engineer approves the prod preview [design].
57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** for on-call engineers to approve any path at 2 a.m., they
65	  must be code owners of every deployable path, which weakens domain review on normal days. No
66	  verified solution yet (Options §1, §7, §8); S7 depends on it. Because on-call approvers only
67	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
68	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
69	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
70	  approver, like L2, but that approver must own the path, and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
71	  the prod preview (OD2, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
72	  for speed.
73	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
74	  business associate, as the brief implies.
75	
76	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
77	
78	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
79	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
80	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
81	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
82	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.
83	
84	### Roles
85	
86	| Role | Rule |
87	|---|---|
88	| Author (engineer + their agent) | Never approves own change; GitHub blocks PR authors from approving (📖 R3.3.1). |
89	| Approver | Always an engineer, never an agent (owner rule, OD5). Named in CODEOWNERS; ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3); for an app-opened PR, ≠ the person who triggered it (⚠️ R3.3.4, layer 5). |
90	| Incident responder | Engineer who diagnoses and writes the fix or the JIT request. Never the on-call approver of the same shift (OD7). |
91	| On-call approver | Engineer on the on-call schedule, primary + backup, 24/7; wait ≤ 15 min (S7). While on call they only approve: they write no fix and file no JIT request, so the approver is always distinct from the author (OD7). The primary approves; the backup replaces an unavailable primary (OD2). No platform-team membership is required; all engineers follow one agreed approval procedure (OD2). |
92	| Data owner [design] | Named per tenant; co-approves real-data reads (layer 6). |
93	| Control owner | DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1); owns policies and metrics; not the only approver. |
94	
95	---
96	
97	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
98	
99	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
100	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
101	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
102	
103	**On Papaya's stack**
104	
105	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
106	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
107	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
108	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
109	  holds.
110	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
111	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
112	    accepted as a process control, D2);
113	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
114	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
115	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
116	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
117	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
118	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
119	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
120	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
121	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
122	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
123	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
124	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
125	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
126	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
127	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
128	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
129	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
130	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
131	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
132	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
133	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
134	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
135	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
136	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
137	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
138	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
139	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
140	    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
141	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (key 📖 R4.4.5; need ⚠️ R4.6 #3);
142	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:userId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
143	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
144	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
145	- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
146	  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
147	- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
148	  environment of the monorepo, in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed,
149	  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
150	- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
151	  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
152	- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
153	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
154	  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
155	  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).
156	
157	**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
158	`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
159	and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
160	(📖 R2.8.1); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.
161	
162	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write, keep fast prod reads and a free non-prod loop.
163	Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls
168	
169	**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
170	and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
171	untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
172	
173	**On Papaya's stack**
174	
175	- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
176	  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
177	  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
178	- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited:
179	
180	  | Key | Value and reason |
181	  |---|---|
182	  | `permissions.defaultMode` | `default` (Manual). A default, not a lock: users can switch to auto; VS Code remembers the last pick (D1, R6.9.3). |
183	  | `permissions.allow` | Read-only commands Papaya uses, to cut prompts (R6.9.3). |
184	  | `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` | `true`, one rule set (D1, research 6.9.4 Q4; R1.2.5). Cost: project and user rules are ignored, so the managed set must carry every deny/ask rule projects need; prompts likely rise (⚠️ research 6.9.4 Q4). |
185	  | `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` | `"disable"`: removes bypass mode (P3a; R1.2.2). Auto mode, where a classifier approves instead of a person, stays available (D1) and is measured through `permission_mode`. |
186	  | `permissions.deny` / `ask` | Deny credential paths (R5.5.4; `Read(...)` syntax ⚠️ R1.8 #5). Ask for `WebFetch`, which the sandbox domain list does not limit (R1.6.2); cost: a prompt per fetch. The HIPAA template denies WebFetch (R5.5.4); "ask" is a deliberate deviation so that documentation lookups still work. |
187	  | `requiredMinimumVersion` | ≥ 2.1.285 for `allowedProviders` (R1.1.15), which also covers `--restricted` (2.1.248, R6.9.1b) and the plugin-pin fix (2.1.179, R6.2.7); ≥ 2.1.295 if any managed hook uses `onFailure: "block"` (R1.5.2); and ≥ the latest fixed advisory at rollout (R6.3.9). It does not end running sessions and fails open on a bad value (R1.1.13). |
188	  | `allowedProviders` + `forceLoginOrgUUID` | `["anthropic"]` + Papaya's org; closes most bypasses on **endpoint-managed** machines (R1.1.15). `forceLoginOrgUUID` checks claude.ai sign-ins only, not Claude Console sign-ins (R5.5.5); with it set, sessions on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `apiKeyHelper` are refused (R1.11.3.11). |
189	  | `allowManagedHooksOnly` | `true` (R1.5.4). |
190	  | sandbox | `sandbox.enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, narrow `network.allowedDomains` locked by `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`; `credentials` / `filesystem.denyRead` on `~/.aws`, which the sandbox can otherwise read (R1.6.3, R1.6.4). |
191	  | MCP, plugins | Layer 4. |
192	  | OTel | Exporter on, content flags `0` (R1.1.20, R5.5.4). |
193	
194	- **Trade-off on AWS credentials [design].** With `~/.aws` hidden from the sandbox, the plan is to
195	  list `aws`, `pulumi` and `serverless` in `sandbox.excludedCommands`. Excluded commands run "with
196	  full access" (📖 R1.6.4), which likely includes the network (⚠️ inference). How the list matches
197	  commands (prefix or text, and chained commands) is not researched (⚠️). So these tools are an
198	  egress channel outside the allowlist, and an injected `aws` command could send out the SSO token
199	  cache itself. That token likely opens every role assigned to the engineer for the rest of the
200	  portal session (📖 R2.1.5; token reuse ⚠️ R2.2.2), probably including JIT or data-read grants added
201	  later in that session (⚠️ inference). Mitigations [design]: a short portal session (📖 R2.1.5); end
202	  the existing portal session and sign in fresh **before** a JIT or data-read grant is created
203	  (whether ending a session invalidates a token already stolen is unverified ⚠️; ending it does not
204	  end role sessions, 📖 R2.4.3); an SCP that denies writes to resources outside Papaya's organization using
205	  `aws:ResourceOrgID` (key 📖 R2.3.8). Residual risk: token theft during a session. It is accepted
206	  because the engineer holds no **standing** prod write and no **standing** PHI read; during a JIT
207	  or data-read window the protection is the process rule in layer 1 (D2). Stronger option, phase 3:
208	  a separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions
209	  (⚠️ R6.5 #2).
210	- **Session types:**
211	
212	  | Session | Identity | Flags | Enforcement |
213	  |---|---|---|---|
214	  | Daily development (laptop) | non-prod roles + `ProdReadMetadata` | baseline | Auto mode by choice (D1); `--restricted` recommended (D3). |
215	  | Incident analysis (laptop) | meant to be `ProdReadMetadata` only | `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"`, started in an empty scratch directory, not the repo [design] | Process rule (D3, research 6.9.4 Q1–Q2). No WebFetch, and file tools confined to the working directory (📖 R6.9.1b); Edit/Write are excluded only if `--tools` acts as an exclusive list (⚠️ unverified), but Bash can still write in its working directory (📖 R1.6.3) and call any role in the cache. |
216	  | CI agent (hosted runner) | own GitHub App token; never `production` | `--restricted`, explicit `--tools`; all rules in a managed-settings file on the runner | Workflow file under CODEOWNERS (D3, research 6.9.4 Q5). The file is advisory if `Bash` is in `--tools` (layer 5). |
217	  | JIT terminal | JIT grant | no agent | Process rule (D2). |
218	  | Auto-mode environment (phase 3) | non-prod only | auto encouraged | D1 option (c). |
219	
220	- **Hard limits:** Bash rules are not a boundary (📖 R1.2.6); hooks fail open unless
221	  `"onFailure": "block"` (📖 R1.5.2); `--restricted` cannot be forced by a setting (📖 R6.9.1), and a `PATH` wrapper on laptops can be bypassed (⚠️ R6.9.1c);
222	  on laptops **without MDM**, a different login, an API key or a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` variable skips
223	  server-managed settings, `allowedProviders` included (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ R1.8 #3, G11). So S5's
224	  "nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed" is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
225	- **Auto memory:** engineers review it and delete it after a suspicious session; residual risk with a
226	  named owner (D3).
227	- **Fallback:** switch to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers auto mode, a serious
228	  advisory appears, or an audit finds auto mode touched a protected scope (D1).
229	
230	**Audit evidence.** Managed settings in git with PR approvals; `/status` and `claude doctor` from
231	sampled machines (📖 R1.1.18); OTel `claude_code.tool_decision` (`permission_mode`) and
232	`claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user` (`duration_ms`, rubber-stamping signal) (fields 📖 research 6.6
233	D1 metrics; thresholds ⚠️). Settings-change audit events on Team: unknown (⚠️ R1.1.12).
234	
235	**Cost / value.** More prompts than auto mode, partly offset by the read-only allowlist. Compliance
236	gets one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices (P3c).
237	
238	---
239	
240	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
241	
242	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
243	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
244	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
245	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
246	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
247	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level. (A PR that
248	touches paths of several owner teams needs an approval from each; a real-data read is not a change
249	and has its own rule, L3-data.) Incidents use the same
250	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
251	
252	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
253	|---|---|---|---|---|
254	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
255	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
256	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
257	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner of the L3 path ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (in incidents: the on-call approver, who is always an owner, see below) | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
258	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b) | layer 7 |
259	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9 | layer 6 |
260	
261	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
262	the whole team (OD3). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need an approval
263	from the owners of those files rather than any code owner.
264	
265	**On Papaya's stack**
266	
267	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
268	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
269	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
270	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
271	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
272	- **L3 approvals [design]:** a path-based rule requires 1 approval from the team that owns each L3
273	  path (📖 R3.2.4); GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). Every on-call approver,
274	  primary and backup, is a member of every L3 owner team for the length of the shift, so a
275	  night-time L3 fix can always be approved. A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5) adds what
276	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
277	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3).
278	- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
279	  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
280	  policy finding it stops. A second PR adds `deploy-approvals/<sha>.yaml` with the
281	  preview hash, approved by an engineer ≠ author (it may be the same approver, who now sees the
282	  prod diff); the job continues only if the hash matches (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). A
283	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
284	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
285	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
286	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
287	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
288	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
289	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
290	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
291	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
292	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
293	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
294	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
295	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
296	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
297	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
298	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
299	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
300	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
301	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
302	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1).
303	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
304	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design].
305	
306	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
307	
308	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
309	unavailable).
310	
311	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
312	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
313	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
314	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
315	3. R reviews the diff, and can catch a missing queue change, then approves. E merges.
316	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
317	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
318	
319	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
320	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.
321	
322	**Cost / value.** One approval for every prod change (from the path owners for risky ones), none
323	in non-prod.
324	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

366	
367	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
368	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
369	checks as human code (S10).
370	
371	**On Papaya's stack**
372	
373	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
374	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
375	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
376	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
377	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
378	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
379	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
380	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
381	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
382	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
383	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
384	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
385	  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
386	    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
387	    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
388	    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
389	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
390	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register.
391	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without

393	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to

395	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).

401	- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,

403	  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).

430	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
431	
432	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
433	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
434	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
435	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
436	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
437	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
438	
439	**On Papaya's stack**
440	
441	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
442	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
443	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
444	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
445	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
446	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
447	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
448	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
449	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
450	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
451	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
452	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
453	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
454	    redacted summary. This
455	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
456	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
457	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
458	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
459	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
460	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
461	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
462	  1.11.4 L6).
463	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default; the auto-mode
464	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
465	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
466	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
467	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
468	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
469	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
470	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is unprotected unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
471	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
472	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
473	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
474	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
475	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule [design; GĐ-14 says only that non-prod is synthetic]. Cost: until scanned, that store is
476	  not part of the free loop.
477	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
478	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
479	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
480	  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
481	  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).
482	
483	**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data (📖 R5.4.3; ⚠️ R5.7 #5);
484	data-read requests and the data-read role's CloudTrail; planted-injection reports (layer 8); non-prod
485	scan results (S11).
486	
487	**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
488	Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2;
489	actions ⚠️ G13) and by process
490	elsewhere, and a record per exception (S9).

495	
496	**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
497	named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
498	is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.
499	
500	**On Papaya's stack**
501	
502	- **Audit stores:**
503	  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
504	    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
505	    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
506	    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
507	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
508	  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
509	  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
510	    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
511	    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
512	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
513	    with an expected copy (G8);
514	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
515	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
516	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
517	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
518	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
519	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
520	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
521	- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
522	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
523	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
524	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
525	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
526	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
527	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
528	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
529	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
530	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
531	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
532	  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
533	  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
534	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
535	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
536	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5).
537	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
538	
539	  | Step | Rule |
540	  |---|---|
541	  | When | The PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. |
542	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
543	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
544	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). |
545	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
546	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
547	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
548	
549	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
550	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
551	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
552	
553	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
554	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
555	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
556	  this draft). On a breach,
557	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
558	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
559	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
560	  (D2, ⚠️).
561	
562	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
563	reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
564	schedule and approval waits (S7).
565	
566	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
567	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
568	incidents, plus detection.
569	
570	---
571	
572	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
573	
574	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
575	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
576	attacks.
577	
578	**On Papaya's stack**
579	
580	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
581	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
582	  Applicability); engineering leads (CODEOWNERS); engineering management (on-call schedule).
583	- **Policy as code:** managed settings, catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are
584	  files under CODEOWNERS; GitHub settings that are not files are compared with an expected copy
585	  (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8). Few GitHub admins, reviewed quarterly.
586	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
587	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
588	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed). Framing Q8 (round 1): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials,
589	  (2) narrow standing prod access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2).
590	
591	  | Phase | Days | Items, in order |
592	  |---|---|---|
593	  | 1 | 0–30 | Measure the incident PR lane on one service (first task, Options §9). Non-prod data scan. OIDC for deploy workflows; remove long-lived keys (except k0s/Firebase under OD1); move laptop deploys to CI (GĐ-10, unconfirmed). Rulesets, CODEOWNERS and its validation check; required S10 checks. `ProdReadMetadata` becomes the only standing prod role (existing broad prod read roles removed); start moving secrets to runtime resolution and redacting logs at source, service by service. On-call approver schedule and a minimal incident-responder schedule (named, 24/7), because on-call approvers only approve (OD7); minimal JIT fallback **with** per-grant CloudTrail comparison and a drift check of the stacks it touched (by hand until automated, as D2 requires); risk stop in the deploy job (the policy-finding trigger works from phase 2); k0s/Firebase deploy credentials moved to `production` environment secrets; **then** remove standing prod write. MCP/plugin catalogue v1. Managed settings, phase-1 subset: `defaultMode` and `disableBypassPermissionsMode` (D1 said "immediately"), the keys that enforce the catalogue (`strictKnownMarketplaces`, `blockedMarketplaces`, `disableSideloadFlags`, `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`) and `requiredMinimumVersion` (needed by the plugin-pin fix). Also the read-only `permissions.allow` list, kept with Manual mode as D1 paired them (OD7b). |

595	  | 3 | 60–90 | Planted-injection test on the real configuration (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.5; ⚠️ R6.5 #12); auto-mode non-prod environment (D1 c); separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions; first ISO evidence pack; 90-day review of D1–D3. |

597	- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
598	- **Standards mapping** (⚠️ R5.6; HIPAA and Vietnam text 📖 R5.2, R5.4; ISO IDs recalled, not read,

602	  |---|---|---|---|
603	  | 1, 6 access | 5.15–5.18, 8.2, 8.3, 8.5 | 164.312(a)(2)(i); 164.308(a)(3)–(4) | Decree 356 Art. 4(2) |
604	  | 3, 5 change | 8.32, 8.31, 8.25, 5.3 | 164.312(c); 164.316(b) | — |

606	  | 4 suppliers | 5.19–5.23 | 164.308(b), 164.314(a) | Law 91 Art. 20 |
607	
608	  "A named human approves" is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement
609	  (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
610	- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.
611	
612	**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files; monthly metrics; 90-day review minutes; exception
613	register; planted-injection reports.
614	
615	**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and the owners of deploy workflows. Compliance gets a managed system

1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
2	
3	> Status: draft v3, for owner review · Updated: 2026-11-09
4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
5	> what it gives Compliance.
6	
7	## How to read this
8	
9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
12	
13	| Marker | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes and links the official page. |
16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
19	
20	Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
21	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
22	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
23	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
24	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
25	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. The decision in one page
30	
31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
33	
34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
35	
36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h, layer 7) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
41	
42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
43	|---|---|
44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, OD1, OD6; storage conditions [design], layer 5). |
46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
48	
49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
50	
51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an engineer approves the prod preview [design].
57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** for on-call engineers to approve any path at 2 a.m., they
65	  must be code owners of every deployable path, which weakens domain review on normal days. No
66	  verified solution yet (Options §1, §7, §8); S7 depends on it. Because on-call approvers only
67	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
68	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
69	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
70	  approver, like L2, but that approver must own the path, and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
71	  the prod preview (OD2, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
72	  for speed.
73	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
74	  business associate, as the brief implies.
75	
76	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
77	
78	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
79	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
80	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
81	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
82	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.
83	
84	### Roles
85	
86	| Role | Rule |
87	|---|---|
88	| Author (engineer + their agent) | Never approves own change; GitHub blocks PR authors from approving (📖 R3.3.1). |
89	| Approver | Always an engineer, never an agent (owner rule, OD5). Named in CODEOWNERS; ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3); for an app-opened PR, ≠ the person who triggered it (⚠️ R3.3.4, layer 5). |
90	| Incident responder | Engineer who diagnoses and writes the fix or the JIT request. Never the on-call approver of the same shift (OD7). |
91	| On-call approver | Engineer on the on-call schedule, primary + backup, 24/7; wait ≤ 15 min (S7). While on call they only approve: they write no fix and file no JIT request, so the approver is always distinct from the author (OD7). The primary approves; the backup replaces an unavailable primary (OD2). No platform-team membership is required; all engineers follow one agreed approval procedure (OD2). |
92	| Data owner [design] | Named per tenant; co-approves real-data reads (layer 6). |
93	| Control owner | DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1); owns policies and metrics; not the only approver. |

97	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
98	
99	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
100	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
101	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
102	
103	**On Papaya's stack**
104	
105	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
106	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
107	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
108	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
109	  holds.
110	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
111	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
112	    accepted as a process control, D2);
113	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
114	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
115	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
116	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
117	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
118	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
119	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
120	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
121	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
122	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
123	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
124	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
125	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
126	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
127	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
128	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
129	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
130	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
131	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
132	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
133	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
134	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
135	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
136	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
137	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
138	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
139	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
140	    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
141	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (key 📖 R4.4.5; need ⚠️ R4.6 #3);
142	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:userId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
143	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
144	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
145	- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
146	  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
147	- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
148	  environment of the monorepo, in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed,
149	  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
150	- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
151	  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
152	- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
153	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
154	  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
155	  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).
156	
157	**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
158	`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
159	and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
160	(📖 R2.8.1); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.
161	
162	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write, keep fast prod reads and a free non-prod loop.
163	Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.

167	## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls
168	
169	**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
170	and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
171	untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
172	
173	**On Papaya's stack**
174	
175	- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
176	  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
177	  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
178	- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited:
179	
180	  | Key | Value and reason |
181	  |---|---|
182	  | `permissions.defaultMode` | `default` (Manual). A default, not a lock: users can switch to auto; VS Code remembers the last pick (D1, R6.9.3). |
183	  | `permissions.allow` | Read-only commands Papaya uses, to cut prompts (R6.9.3). |
184	  | `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` | `true`, one rule set (D1, research 6.9.4 Q4; R1.2.5). Cost: project and user rules are ignored, so the managed set must carry every deny/ask rule projects need; prompts likely rise (⚠️ research 6.9.4 Q4). |
185	  | `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` | `"disable"`: removes bypass mode (P3a; R1.2.2). Auto mode, where a classifier approves instead of a person, stays available (D1) and is measured through `permission_mode`. |
186	  | `permissions.deny` / `ask` | Deny credential paths (R5.5.4; `Read(...)` syntax ⚠️ R1.8 #5). Ask for `WebFetch`, which the sandbox domain list does not limit (R1.6.2); cost: a prompt per fetch. The HIPAA template denies WebFetch (R5.5.4); "ask" is a deliberate deviation so that documentation lookups still work. |
187	  | `requiredMinimumVersion` | ≥ 2.1.285 for `allowedProviders` (R1.1.15), which also covers `--restricted` (2.1.248, R6.9.1b) and the plugin-pin fix (2.1.179, R6.2.7); ≥ 2.1.295 if any managed hook uses `onFailure: "block"` (R1.5.2); and ≥ the latest fixed advisory at rollout (R6.3.9). It does not end running sessions and fails open on a bad value (R1.1.13). |
188	  | `allowedProviders` + `forceLoginOrgUUID` | `["anthropic"]` + Papaya's org; closes most bypasses on **endpoint-managed** machines (R1.1.15). `forceLoginOrgUUID` checks claude.ai sign-ins only, not Claude Console sign-ins (R5.5.5); with it set, sessions on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `apiKeyHelper` are refused (R1.11.3.11). |
189	  | `allowManagedHooksOnly` | `true` (R1.5.4). |
190	  | sandbox | `sandbox.enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, narrow `network.allowedDomains` locked by `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`; `credentials` / `filesystem.denyRead` on `~/.aws`, which the sandbox can otherwise read (R1.6.3, R1.6.4). |
191	  | MCP, plugins | Layer 4. |
192	  | OTel | Exporter on, content flags `0` (R1.1.20, R5.5.4). |
193	
194	- **Trade-off on AWS credentials [design].** With `~/.aws` hidden from the sandbox, the plan is to
195	  list `aws`, `pulumi` and `serverless` in `sandbox.excludedCommands`. Excluded commands run "with
196	  full access" (📖 R1.6.4), which likely includes the network (⚠️ inference). How the list matches
197	  commands (prefix or text, and chained commands) is not researched (⚠️). So these tools are an
198	  egress channel outside the allowlist, and an injected `aws` command could send out the SSO token
199	  cache itself. That token likely opens every role assigned to the engineer for the rest of the
200	  portal session (📖 R2.1.5; token reuse ⚠️ R2.2.2), probably including JIT or data-read grants added
201	  later in that session (⚠️ inference). Mitigations [design]: a short portal session (📖 R2.1.5); end
202	  the existing portal session and sign in fresh **before** a JIT or data-read grant is created
203	  (whether ending a session invalidates a token already stolen is unverified ⚠️; ending it does not
204	  end role sessions, 📖 R2.4.3); an SCP that denies writes to resources outside Papaya's organization using
205	  `aws:ResourceOrgID` (key 📖 R2.3.8). Residual risk: token theft during a session. It is accepted
206	  because the engineer holds no **standing** prod write and no **standing** PHI read; during a JIT
207	  or data-read window the protection is the process rule in layer 1 (D2). Stronger option, phase 3:
208	  a separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions
209	  (⚠️ R6.5 #2).
210	- **Session types:**
211	
212	  | Session | Identity | Flags | Enforcement |
213	  |---|---|---|---|
214	  | Daily development (laptop) | non-prod roles + `ProdReadMetadata` | baseline | Auto mode by choice (D1); `--restricted` recommended (D3). |
215	  | Incident analysis (laptop) | meant to be `ProdReadMetadata` only | `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"`, started in an empty scratch directory, not the repo [design] | Process rule (D3, research 6.9.4 Q1–Q2). No WebFetch, and file tools confined to the working directory (📖 R6.9.1b); Edit/Write are excluded only if `--tools` acts as an exclusive list (⚠️ unverified), but Bash can still write in its working directory (📖 R1.6.3) and call any role in the cache. |
216	  | CI agent (hosted runner) | own GitHub App token; never `production` | `--restricted`, explicit `--tools`; all rules in a managed-settings file on the runner | Workflow file under CODEOWNERS (D3, research 6.9.4 Q5). The file is advisory if `Bash` is in `--tools` (layer 5). |
217	  | JIT terminal | JIT grant | no agent | Process rule (D2). |
218	  | Auto-mode environment (phase 3) | non-prod only | auto encouraged | D1 option (c). |
219	
220	- **Hard limits:** Bash rules are not a boundary (📖 R1.2.6); hooks fail open unless
221	  `"onFailure": "block"` (📖 R1.5.2); `--restricted` cannot be forced by a setting (📖 R6.9.1), and a `PATH` wrapper on laptops can be bypassed (⚠️ R6.9.1c);
222	  on laptops **without MDM**, a different login, an API key or a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` variable skips

224	  "nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed" is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
225	- **Auto memory:** engineers review it and delete it after a suspicious session; residual risk with a
226	  named owner (D3).
227	- **Fallback:** switch to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers auto mode, a serious
228	  advisory appears, or an audit finds auto mode touched a protected scope (D1).

232	`claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user` (`duration_ms`, rubber-stamping signal) (fields 📖 research 6.6

240	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
241	
242	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
243	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
244	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
245	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
246	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
247	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level. (A PR that
248	touches paths of several owner teams needs an approval from each; a real-data read is not a change
249	and has its own rule, L3-data.) Incidents use the same
250	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
251	
252	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
253	|---|---|---|---|---|
254	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
255	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
256	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
257	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner of the L3 path ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (in incidents: the on-call approver, who is always an owner, see below) | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
258	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b) | layer 7 |
259	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9 | layer 6 |
260	
261	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
262	the whole team (OD3). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need an approval
263	from the owners of those files rather than any code owner.
264	
265	**On Papaya's stack**
266	
267	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
268	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
269	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
270	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
271	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
272	- **L3 approvals [design]:** a path-based rule requires 1 approval from the team that owns each L3
273	  path (📖 R3.2.4); GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). Every on-call approver,
274	  primary and backup, is a member of every L3 owner team for the length of the shift, so a
275	  night-time L3 fix can always be approved. A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5) adds what
276	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
277	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3).
278	- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
279	  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
280	  policy finding it stops. A second PR adds `deploy-approvals/<sha>.yaml` with the
281	  preview hash, approved by an engineer ≠ author (it may be the same approver, who now sees the
282	  prod diff); the job continues only if the hash matches (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). A
283	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
284	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
285	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
286	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
287	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
288	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
289	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
290	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
291	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
292	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
293	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
294	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
295	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
296	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
297	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
298	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
299	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
300	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
301	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
302	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1).
303	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
304	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design].
305	
306	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
307	
308	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
309	unavailable).
310	
311	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
312	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
313	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
314	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
315	3. R reviews the diff, and can catch a missing queue change, then approves. E merges.
316	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
317	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
318	
319	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
320	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.
321	
322	**Cost / value.** One approval for every prod change (from the path owners for risky ones), none
323	in non-prod.
324	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

331	Only reviewed, pinned entries from a catalogue are allowed. The catalogue is the inventory (P4c).
332	Review takes ≤ 5 working days (S6), or people work around it.
333	
334	**On Papaya's stack**
335

337	  pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only). Managed `strictKnownMarketplaces` = Papaya only,
338	  `blockedMarketplaces`, `enabledPlugins: false` to pull one (📖 R1.4.2), checked before download and
339	  at session start (📖 R1.4.3). `disableSideloadFlags` rejects `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`,
340	  `--agents`, `--mcp-config` but not `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add` (📖 R1.4.2). With
341	  `allowManagedHooksOnly`, plugin hooks run only for force-enabled plugins (📖 R1.5.4). User mods are
342	  blocked by the `allowManagedModsOnly` option under `pluginConfigs` → `cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin`
343	  → `options` (📖 R1.5.6). The version floor covers the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).

365	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
366	
367	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
368	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
369	checks as human code (S10).
370	
371	**On Papaya's stack**
372	
373	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
374	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
375	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
376	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
377	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
378	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
379	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
380	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
381	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
382	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
383	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
384	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
385	  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
386	    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
387	    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
388	    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
389	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
390	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register.
391	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
392	  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
393	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
394	  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
395	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
396	- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
397	  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).

399	  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA"; the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
400	  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5; conclusion [design]).
401	- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
402	  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5); CI validates the file, because
403	  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
404	- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
405	  📖 R3.5.4).
406	- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
407	  requests (📖 R1.7.8); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);

409	  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
410	  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
411	  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),

417	  Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1); Pulumi policy packs (📖 R4.2.2).
